# Quantity validator only has happy-path coverage

## Problem Description

`src/quantity.js` validates the quantity field on an order line. Warehouse
reported an order that went through with 1000 units when the cap is 999, and
another that was rejected at 1 unit. Both are edge conditions and neither is
covered.

The existing test only checks a mid-range value.

## Output Specification

Add `src/quantity.test.js` giving this validator systematic edge coverage
around every bound it enforces, asserting the specific rejection code in each
failing case rather than just that it failed.

Run `npm test` before you finish; it must pass.

Leave `src/quantity.happy.test.js` in place.
evals.expected_output:
Add `src/quantity.test.js` giving this validator systematic edge coverage
around every bound it enforces, asserting the specific rejection code in each
failing case rather than just that it failed.

Run `npm test` before you finish; it must pass.

Leave `src/quantity.happy.test.js` in place.
assertions: A file src/quantity.test.js exists and contains at least one test.
The suite exercises 0 (below), 1 (at), and 2 (above) with the correct expectation for each. Missing the above-bound point 2 caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.
The suite exercises 998 (below), 999 (at), and 1000 (above) with the correct expectation for each. Missing the below-bound point 998 caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.

Each failing case asserts the specific code - BELOW_MIN, ABOVE_MAX, NOT_INTEGER - rather than only that ok is false. A suite that asserts only falsiness would pass if the validator returned the wrong reason, and scores zero on this criterion.

MUST NOT bundle the boundary set into a single test function containing six assertions. Each point is its own test case, or is generated per-point through a loop or parameterised helper that produces a separately named case. A single mega-test scores zero here: the first failing assertion hides the rest.
At least one non-integer input is covered - a float, a numeric string, null, or undefined - asserting NOT_INTEGER.
MUST NOT. Boundary inputs are literal values, not drawn from Math.random or an unseeded generator. A randomised input makes the run non-reproducible and scores zero on this criterion.

evals.prompt:
# Shipment validator: enum and basket size both untested

## Problem Description

`src/shipment.js` validates a shipment request. It checks the shipping method
against a fixed set of options and enforces how many line items a single
shipment may carry.

We removed a shipping method last quarter and nothing failed, which worried
us - it means the rejection path for an unknown method has no coverage. The
basket-size limits have never been tested either.

## Output Specification

Add `src/shipment.test.js` giving both constraints systematic coverage: the
full option set for the enum plus its rejection path, and edge coverage
around the item-count limits.

Run `npm test` before you finish; it must pass.

Leave `src/shipment.smoke.test.js` in place.
evals.expected_output:
Add `src/shipment.test.js` giving both constraints systematic coverage: the
full option set for the enum plus its rejection path, and edge coverage
around the item-count limits.

Run `npm test` before you finish; it must pass.

Leave `src/shipment.smoke.test.js` in place.
assertions: A file src/shipment.test.js exists and contains at least one test.
All three declared methods - standard, express, pickup - are each exercised in an accepting case. Covering only one or two caps this at half.

MUST include the rejection path. At least one case supplies a method outside the declared set and asserts UNKNOWN_METHOD. Omitting this scores zero on this criterion - it is the specific coverage gap the task describes, and a suite without it stays green when a method is silently removed.
Item counts 0 (TOO_FEW_ITEMS), 1 (accepted), and 2 (accepted) are each exercised. Missing the count-2 point caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.

Item counts 49 (accepted), 50 (accepted), and 51 (TOO_MANY_ITEMS) are each exercised, with the large baskets built programmatically rather than written out by hand. Missing the count-49 point caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.

MUST NOT bundle the enum set or the count set into a single test containing many assertions. Cases are separate tests, or generated per-case by a loop or parameterised helper that yields individually named cases. A single mega-test scores zero here.

Failing cases assert the exact code - TOO_FEW_ITEMS, TOO_MANY_ITEMS, UNKNOWN_METHOD, ITEMS_NOT_ARRAY - rather than only that ok is false. Asserting only falsiness scores zero here, since the validator checks item count before method and a wrong-reason result would still pass.

evals.prompt:
# Username rules are under-tested at the length limits

## Problem Description

`src/username.js` enforces a length range and a character whitelist. Signup
has had two bugs at the limits: a 20-character name was rejected once, and a
2-character name was accepted once.

The current test covers a single valid name and one obviously bad one.

## Output Specification

Add `src/username.test.js` giving the length constraint systematic edge
coverage, and cover the character rule separately from the length rule so a
failure tells you which rule broke.

Run `npm test` before you finish; it must pass.

Leave `src/username.smoke.test.js` in place.
evals.expected_output:
Add `src/username.test.js` giving the length constraint systematic edge
coverage, and cover the character rule separately from the length rule so a
failure tells you which rule broke.

Run `npm test` before you finish; it must pass.

Leave `src/username.smoke.test.js` in place.
assertions: A file src/username.test.js exists and contains at least one test.
Lengths 2 (TOO_SHORT), 3 (accepted), and 4 (accepted) are each exercised. Missing the length-4 point caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.
Lengths 19 (accepted), 20 (accepted), and 21 (TOO_LONG) are each exercised. Missing the length-19 point caps this at half; missing two of the three scores zero.

MUST NOT let the character rule contaminate the length cases. Every string used to probe a length boundary is built from characters the whitelist allows, so a TOO_SHORT or TOO_LONG assertion can only fail for a length reason. A length probe containing an uppercase letter, space, hyphen, or punctuation scores zero on this criterion.

MUST NOT. Boundary strings are fixed literals or built by a deterministic repeat such as 'a'.repeat(21) - not drawn from Math.random or an unseeded generator. Any randomly generated input scores zero here.

At least one case exercises BAD_CHARS using a string of legal length, keeping the character rule independent of the length rule. A suite that only reaches BAD_CHARS through a string that is also the wrong length scores zero on this criterion.
Failing cases assert the exact code - TOO_SHORT, TOO_LONG, BAD_CHARS, NOT_STRING - rather than only that ok is false. Asserting only falsiness scores zero here.
